title: kate-core: name a file that came back
summary: reload_prompt_line says the file came back when the disk change is Created. A modified file and a deleted file keep their sentences. Linux CI runs the test.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition: pub fn reload_prompt_line(file: Option<&FileState>, dirty: bool) -> Option<&'static str>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: In reload_prompt_line, match DiskChange::Created and return Some with the sentence The file on disk came back. Do this for a clean buffer and a dirty buffer. Deleted still returns The file on disk is gone. A missing file still returns None. A clean modified file still returns Reload the file from disk. A dirty modified file still returns The file on disk changed. Quiet still returns None. Leave reload_choice unchanged. The test a_created_file_says_the_file_came_back sets disk_change to Created on a FileState from file_state. Both dirty false and dirty true return The file on disk came back. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep this change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: document::tests::a_created_file_says_the_file_came_back
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. A clean Created file returns Reload the file from disk. A dirty Created file returns The file on disk changed. After the change both return The file on disk came back.
